text:
alex: heads up — customer MapleHealth escalated. They say audit exports for the Feb retention window never arrived. asking for timeline + whether KMS/HSM was involved. cc @maya @jordan :eyes:

sam: i'm on repro. export job hits 500 on /internal/audit/export?customer=maplehealth. tail of exporter logs:
```
2026-03-14T02:11:58Z exporter INFO starting export job id=exp-993
2026-03-14T02:12:12Z exporter ERROR export failed status=403 error=AccessDenied KMS key access denied key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/maple-health-prod requestId=abc123
2026-03-14T02:12:12Z exporter INFO aborting job id=exp-993
```

maya: do we know if MapleHealth is on KMS-managed keys (HSM-backed) or our default envelope keys?

security-bot: KMS access logs: key=maple-health-prod, principal=exporter-service@redwood-inference, result=DENY, ts=2026-03-14T02:12:12Z, req=abc123. Key is customer-specific, HSM-protected (Customer-managed key).

jordan: quick context: infra ran a config rollout around 02:00UTC to rotate exporter instances (patch + instance refresh). there was a transient IAM binding issue on the exporter role; some instances lost permission for KMS access until binding replayed. that matches the 403 window. exporter currently treats 403 as fatal and doesn't queue retry.

alex: ok — action plan proposal: 1) re-run the export for the affected window, 2) add retry on 403 for export path with backoff (short-term patch), 3) confirm key binding replay and add guard to avoid instance refresh during exports, 4) final customer note.

lina-legal: wording: avoid 'we lost data' or definitive claims until we confirm re-run results. prefer 'delayed delivery of audit export for X to Y'. keep remediation plan and offer artifacts.

sam: repro steps for eng to re-run: 
1) API: POST /internal/audit/export/retry {"job_id":"exp-993"} 
2) Or via k8s job: kubectl -n exports create job --from=cronjob/export-run export-rerun-<ts> 
3) watch logs: kubectl logs -f deploy/exporter | grep exp-993

jordan: i'm running the re-export now, will monitor KMS calls and post progress here. priority -> re-export + verify checksums. ETA ~30m. :thumbsup:

alex: customer comm draft (suggested):
"Hi MapleHealth — we identified a delayed delivery for your audit export covering 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-01 due to a transient permissions issue during an internal deployment. We are re-running the export now and will provide the verification artifact (checksums + signed manifest) and an ETA within 2 hours. We apologize for the disruption and are patching our retry/guard logic to prevent recurrence."

lina-legal: tweak: change 'permissions issue during an internal deployment' -> 'transient permissions issue during an internal maintenance operation'. otherwise ok.

maya: also flag to compliance: retention policy query — were any logs outside retention window permanently deleted? my read: no deletions, only delivery failure. need confirmation after export completes.

sam: i'll prepare CS message and CV (internal incident note) template with timeline and artifacts to hand to customer once we have success.

security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427, severity=P2, owner=jordan, linked_resources=[exp-993, key=maple-health-prod].

jordan: re-export succeeded. verification: checksum match=OK, manifest signed by export-service at 2026-03-14T02:42:03Z. Upload location: s3://redwood-exports/maplehealth/2026-02.

alex: great. sam/lina — please send the customer note (use legal phrasing) and attach manifest + checksums. close loop in ticket and add postmortem if customer requests.

sam: sending now. will paste message in support ticket when sent.

alex: thanks everyone. follow-up: schedule a small dev task to change export retry logic and add pre-rotation IAM validation in infra runbooks.

jordan: noted, will open an internal PR and link INC-2026-0427.

maya: leaving a note for compliance to verify retention flags once more: compliance@redwood — please confirm no retention deletions occurred during maintenance window.

alex: closing here after customer ack. :white_check_mark:
